inline_comments.comment: `@ts-ignore` must be accompanied by an inline comment explaining which TypeScript error is being suppressed and why it cannot be fixed properly. Per project rules, `@ts-ignore` should never be used without that explanation. The underlying type mismatch (likely that the initial `select('.mermaidTooltip')` returns a different `Selection` generic than the `select('body').append('div')` chain) should be fixed by typing `tooltipElem` up-front as `select<HTMLDivElement, unknown>('.mermaidTooltip')`, mirroring the approach already taken in `classDb.ts`.

This block unconditionally appends a new `div.mermaidTooltip` to `<body>` every time `setupToolTips` is called, completely bypassing the existence guard at the top of the function. This is both a DOM leak and a logic error:

1. **DOM leak:** On every subsequent diagram render, a new tooltip `<div>` accumulates in `<body>`. After N renders there will be N+1 tooltip divs in the DOM.
2. **Closure capture:** Because `tooltipElem` is a `let` binding and JS closures capture the binding (not a snapshot), the event handlers established earlier in the function will dereference this new element when they fire — meaning the first, conditionally-created div is orphaned and never shown.

The inline styles should instead be added to the existing conditional creation block at the top of the function (`if (...[0][0] === null)`), so they are applied only once and only when a new tooltip element is actually needed.

The selector was narrowed from `svg.selectAll('g.node')` to all `<g>` elements that carry a `title` attribute. In a class diagram SVG the title attribute can appear on container groups, subgraph wrappers, edge paths, and other non-node elements. Attaching `mouseover`/`mouseout` handlers to those elements can cause tooltip flicker or incorrect tooltip content when the cursor crosses an edge or a group boundary. The original `g.node` selector was intentional — it targeted only node groups. Prefer restoring the specific selector and ensuring node elements carry the appropriate class, rather than broadening the selection.

The background color `#ffffde` and border `1px solid #333` are hardcoded. The flowchart diagram's `styles.ts` defines the same properties using theme variables: `background: ${options.tertiaryColor}` and `border: 1px solid ${options.border2}`. With hardcoded values the class diagram tooltip will look inconsistent or incorrect in dark, forest, and neutral themes. The correct fix is to add a `.mermaidTooltip` CSS rule to the class diagram's `styles.js` using the same theme-variable substitution pattern, rather than inlining literal colour values.

`escapeHtml` is a private instance method that never references `this`. Per project conventions, private class methods that have no dependency on instance state should be extracted as module-level functions. Since this is generic HTML escaping it is also a good candidate for a shared utility: check whether `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/common/common.ts` or `packages/mermaid/src/utils.ts` already expose an equivalent helper before adding a duplicate. (Note: the existing `sanitizeText` in `common.ts` uses DOMPurify and requires a `MermaidConfig` argument, so it serves a different purpose — a lightweight `escapeHtml` module-level export would be the right addition.)

Changed from `if (title === null)` to the falsy check `if (!title)`. The project rules require strict equality (`=== null` / `!= null`) rather than truthy/falsy tests when detecting whether an optional value is absent, to avoid silently treating `''` (or `0` for numeric values) as missing. For a tooltip title specifically, an empty string is likely also invalid, but the intent is clearer and more consistent with project style as `if (title == null)`, which covers both `null` and `undefined` without also swallowing `''`.

general_comments.comment: The inline tooltip styles added in both `classDb.ts` and `flowDb.ts` are missing `font-family`. The existing `.mermaidTooltip` CSS rule in `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/flowchart/styles.ts` includes `font-family: ${options.fontFamily}` so the configured diagram font is applied. Omitting it from the inline styles means the class diagram tooltip (and the flowchart tooltip, once the duplicate-creation bug is fixed) falls back to the browser's default sans-serif rather than the font the user or theme configured.

The inline style block for `.mermaidTooltip` is copy-pasted identically into `classDb.ts` and `flowDb.ts`. If tooltip appearance needs changing in the future, both files must be updated in sync. Extract a shared helper — e.g. `createTooltipElement(): Selection<HTMLDivElement, unknown, HTMLElement, unknown>` in a common tooltip utility module — and call it from both DB classes. This also makes the theme-variable colour issue (see inline comments) a single fix rather than two.

The two `setupToolTips` implementations in `flowDb.ts` and `classDb.ts` are now further out of sync with each other: `classDb.ts` uses `tooltipElem.empty()` while `flowDb.ts` still uses the `(tooltipElem._groups || tooltipElem)[0][0] === null` hack; `classDb.ts` targets `g.node`-equivalent elements via a filter while `flowDb.ts` uses `g.node` directly; and their HTML-rendering paths differ (`.text()` + post-hoc `.html()` in flowchart vs `escapeHtml` + `.html()` in class). These divergences make it easy for future changes to accidentally re-introduce the positioning bug in one but not the other. The shared helper mentioned above would also be the right place to consolidate this logic.
